title: Design tokens
purpose: Named, reusable values for renders and shaders, so independently produced output still looks like it came from one system. These are defaults and suggested ranges, not hard requirements -- every one is meant to be overridden when a piece calls for it.
usage_note: Tokens are advisory. A shader that ignores every palette here is fine if it looks good; the point is that a shader which does not care gets a coherent default instead of an arbitrary one.

thumb.use: fast iteration; roughly 1/16 the cost of 1080p

uhd.use: expensive; supersampling matters less as resolution rises

still.use: print or poster; supersampling is cheap for one frame

cost_model.note: Shading cost scales as width * height * frames * samples^2. Use this to predict a render before starting it.

samples_guidance.1: Correct for shaders whose edges are analytically antialiased. Always try this first.
samples_guidance.2: 4x cost. Removes most visible aliasing in noise and thin features. The usual choice for delivery.
samples_guidance.3: 9x cost. Diminishing returns except on high-contrast thin lines.

timing.loop_rule: Drive animation from u.phase in [0,1), scaled by TAU. Every frequency multiplying phase must be an integer or the loop will not close.

easing.note: Easings for a value in [0,1]. Linear motion reads as mechanical; almost everything benefits from at least smoothstep.

palettes.note: Cosine palettes, evaluated as col = bias + amp * cos(TAU * (freq * t + phase)) for t in [0,1]. They are always in gamut, need no table, and have no interpolation seams. Tune by editing four vec3s.

accents.note: Literal sRGB triples for the rare case where a specific colour is wanted, e.g. a UI-like element inside a render.

black_floor.why: keeps shadows from reading as holes and makes banding visible enough to fix

white_rolloff.why: compresses unbounded accumulation into [0,1) without a hard clip

exposure.why: the single most useful knob to expose; multiply before the tonemap

tone.gamma_note: Output bytes are written with no gamma conversion, matching GLSL and Shadertoy. Values are treated as already display-referred. If a shader does physically-based lighting in linear space, apply pow(col, 1/2.2) itself.

centered_aspect.why: resolution-independent and the convention almost all shader code assumes

pixel.why: when a size must be exact in pixels, e.g. a 1px line

geometry.origin: FC has its origin at the BOTTOM-left with pixel centres at +0.5, matching GLSL. PPM rows are written top-down, so the runtime flips. --top-left-origin disables the flip.

line_widths_in_p_units.note: one pixel is 2/resolution.y in centered_aspect units; use texel_from_height()

frequency.note: in centered_aspect units; frequency is cycles across the half-height

octaves.note: cost is linear; the CPU can afford more than a GPU

lacunarity.note: exactly 2.0 can produce faint axis-aligned alignment; 1.93 avoids it

warp_strength.note: domain warping is the cheapest route from bland fbm to something structural

loop_radius.note: how far the field travels around its circular loop path; larger means more change per loop

bits_per_pixel_per_second.note: synthetic gradients compress much better than camera footage

gif.use: short loops; requires a palettegen stage

png.use: stills; needs an ffmpeg built with zlib

ppm.use: raw stream passthrough for inspection or a custom encoder
